What are executions (and why are they more powerful than on other products)?
Executions are much more powerful than the ‘operations’ or ‘tasks’ that you’re billed on in other products.
An execution is a single run of your entire workflow. It doesn’t matter how many steps are in the workflow or how much data it processes. It’s still a single execution.

This makes your usage more predictable than other tools where you pay individually for every step or task. Plus n8n workflows you can do things in a single execution that would take 10,000 operations in other tools.

Case Study: Automated Production Planning with n8n | Frontkit Studio

The company makes its own products and ships them from a 3PL warehouse. Its plan lives in a manufacturing ERP, purchasing in an inventory planning tool and Odoo, and stock in the warehouse system. We built the n8n workflows that keep those systems in step, so the plan is ready when the team starts.

Someone checked stock against reorder points, then created the purchase order in one tool and the manufacturing order in another. The production lead assigned the day's orders to operators before the shift started.
Finished orders sometimes missed their packaging bookings, and warehouse receipts sometimes arrived without a batch number. Both only surfaced when stock counts or traceability checks did not add up.

When an item drops below its reorder point, the workflow works out how much to make and when, then creates a purchase order in the inventory planning tool and a linked manufacturing order in the ERP. If the manufacturing order fails, Slack hears about it.
Every weekday at 06:00, the workflow freezes the day's plan and assigns each manufacturing order to the right operator. It never overwrites an assignment a person made by hand.

Every morning, finished orders that are missing packaging bookings get them added, but only when the warehouse receipts match what was made. Each booking is read back to confirm it. Anything that does not match goes to Slack.

At 08:00, the workflow checks goods received at the warehouse for a valid batch number and switches batch tracking back on where it was turned off. Traceability gaps show up the next morning instead of during an audit.

The History and Ownership of n8n: Funding, Valuation, and Revenue
The n8n valuation, round by round: who funded n8n, who owns it, how much revenue it makes, and what the numbers do and don't tell you.

Those three numbers are why the subject is confusing. Headlines mix up the valuation, the money raised, and the revenue, and they treat a private funding mark as if it were a market price. The figures also come from different announcements, in different currencies, with different definitions of "customer".

What follows separates them. You get every funding round in order, the revenue that n8n has disclosed, who holds the equity, and how the number compares with n8n's closest peers. You also get the parts that are unknown or contested, stated as such.
it does not tell you n8n's revenue, profit, or how much cash it holds. Those are separate numbers, and only some have been disclosed.

A private company's valuation is not measured the way a listed company's market cap is. There is no daily trading, so the number only moves when shares change hands in a disclosed deal. Each funding round sets a new price, and press coverage multiplies that price across the share count to get the headline.
is the company's worth before that cash arrives.

The second reading is that the mark is a ceiling set by the most optimistic buyer in a single deal. Venture rounds often carry terms that protect the new investor, so the headline price per share can overstate what common shares are worth. A strategic investor may also pay more because the deal comes with a commercial partnership attached, as SAP's did.

Some numbers look like valuations and are not. Total funding raised, about $240 million through the Series C, is the cash that went into the company. Annual recurring revenue, which passed $40 million in mid-2025, is a measure of sales.

The growth figures n8n disclosed track that shift. At the Series B in March 2025, it reported more than 230,000 active users and five times ARR growth. By the Series C term sheet in August 2025, ARR had passed $40 million, which the company described as roughly ten times year-on-year growth, with users up about six times.

The reported valuation was around €250 million. Some secondary sources convert that to roughly $288 million, which is the same mark expressed in dollars rather than a different one. At the announcement, n8n reported more than 230,000 active users and five times ARR growth.
The jump from about €250 million to $2.5 billion in seven months is roughly tenfold. It lines up with the revenue growth n8n reported over the same stretch, which is covered in the next section.
n8n Revenue

n8n is a private company and does not publish accounts the way a listed company would. What is known about n8n revenue comes from figures the company chose to share at funding announcements. There are only a few of them, and each needs its date attached.

The main figure is annual recurring revenue. n8n's ARR passed $40 million around August 2025, when the Series C term sheet was signed. The company described this as about ten times year-on-year growth, and at the Series B seven months earlier it had reported five times ARR growth without a dollar figure.
ARR is not the same as revenue in a set of accounts. It is the annualised value of recurring contracts at a point in time.
A company with $40 million in ARR in August may have booked far less than that over the previous twelve months. For a business growing ten times a year, the gap between the two can be large.

No newer ARR figure had been disclosed as of October 2026. The SAP announcement in May 2026 gave user and customer counts but no revenue number. Any figure you see for n8n's 2026 revenue is an outside estimate, unless it links to an n8n statement.
Where the revenue comes from

n8n has not published how its revenue splits between cloud subscriptions, enterprise licences and any embedded or partner deals. Breakdowns that circulate online are third-party estimates. Check current prices at
The n8n revenue multiple

Putting the two disclosed numbers together gives a rough ratio. A $2.5 billion valuation against $40 million in ARR is about 62 times ARR. That uses the closest pair of dated figures, and it ignores any growth between August and October 2025.
There is no matching figure for the $5.2 billion mark, because no ARR was published alongside it. Any multiple quoted for the SAP round depends on an assumed revenue number, so treat it as a guess.

n8n（エヌエイトエヌ）は、様々なWebサービスやアプリケーションを連携させ、一連の作業を自動化するためのツールです。
コードを書くことなく、画面上での操作のみで自動化の仕組みを構築できます。
機能を持った「ノード」と呼ばれるブロックを配置し、それらを線で繋いで一連の作業の流れ（ワークフロー）を作成します。
